technical_and_design_decisions: Container-side cleanup of RabbitMQ resources using RabbitManagementTemplate (or RabbitAdmin) when 'stream destroy --clean' is invoked; delete queues/bindings/exchanges only when no remaining consumers, with warning if messages remain.

Spring Security with Spring Boot used to secure REST endpoints, DSL shell, and Admin UI; configured via external properties (e.g., xd.security.*); default unsecured if not configured.

Status notifications implemented via client-side polling API plus server-side event propagation over the existing message bus to admin, which pushes to UI via SSE/WebSocket.
SFTP source module uses Spring Integration SFTP adapter; ElasticSearch sink uses Spring Data Elasticsearch or High Level REST Client.
Documentation for ${xd.stream.name}, ${xd.job.name}, ${xd.container.id} and other placeholders added to official docs.

technical_and_design_decisions: Queue/topic cleanup will be performed on the container side (not admin) using RabbitAdmin.getQueueProperties and RabbitManagementTemplate if needed, triggered by an optional '--clean' flag on the stream destroy command.

activities.activity_name: Final system test and doc review
activities.activity_description: End-to-end testing, documentation review, and minor fixes.

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Go and the existing Hyperledger Fabric modular architecture (gRPC, protobuf) as the implementation basis.
Friendly name stored as chaincode metadata mapped to chaincode ID per channel, not replacing internal IDs.
Lifecycle system chaincode extended with deployment policy structures persisted in world state and evaluated on instantiate/upgrade.

Solo orderer implemented as a consensus plugin using a buffered channel, a single sequencing goroutine, and an in-RAM ledger (slice of blocks) with mutex protection; Deliver supports SeekOldest/SeekNewest and replay.
State cache implemented as an in-memory LRU cache inside the peer transaction simulator with invalidation on block commit.
CLI extracted into a separate Go module that only uses generated gRPC clients, removing RocksDB and peer internal dependencies.
Documentation built with Sphinx and published as a static site to hyperledger.org.
GitHub mirror implemented via scheduled git fetch from Gerrit and push to GitHub, read-only.
assumptions: Base Hyperledger Fabric codebase builds and is available for extension.
Developer is experienced with Go, Hyperledger Fabric, and distributed systems.
Solo orderer is intended for development/testing only, not production fault tolerance.
State cache is per-peer and does not require cross-peer coherence beyond existing consensus.
Friendly names are unique per channel.
Windows and Mac build toolchains are available for cross-compilation of the CLI.
Existing CI can be extended for mirroring and docs publishing.
Estimates cover implementation, unit/integration testing, and documentation authoring but exclude long-term maintenance.

Validate correctness and performance of the state cache under concurrent submissions and commits.

Perform end-to-end integration tests across all new features (friendly names, policies, solo orderer, state cache, CLI) and verify build on target platforms.

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement in Go using existing Hyperledger Fabric modular interfaces (gRPC, pluggable orderer/consensus).
Solo orderer implemented as a new ordering service type with an in-memory buffered channel, single batching goroutine, and an in-RAM ledger supporting Seek for history discovery.
Extend the existing Lifecycle System Chaincode (LSCC) to store a friendly name-to-chaincode-ID mapping and deployment/endorsement policies in chaincode metadata.
State cache implemented as an in-memory LRU cache inside the endorsing peer to accelerate rw-set construction, with invalidation on block commit.

Extract CLI into a standalone 'fabric-cli' Go module that uses gRPC client stubs to peers/orderers, removing dependencies on peer internals such as RocksDB, and cross-compile for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
Publish code to GitHub via an automated mirror of the Gerrit repository.
Author documentation in Markdown and publish to the Hyperledger documentation site / GitHub Pages for easy discovery.
assumptions: A single experienced Go developer performs all work; effort estimates are person-days (8-hour workdays).
Existing Fabric build, test, and CI infrastructure is available and reused.
Solo orderer requires only RAM persistence as specified, with no crash recovery.
Friendly chaincode names are unique per channel.
State cache is local per peer and not distributed.
Permissions to create the GitHub mirror and publish documentation are available.
Testing covers unit and basic integration tests, not large-scale performance or load testing.

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement NIO toggle as a boolean property in deploy.properties read during Mule startup, switching the transport stack to NIO-based connectors.
Implement WebSocket support as a new Mule module using the Jetty WebSocket library, exposing inbound/outbound WebSocket endpoints as flow components.
Implement Registry pairing via a REST client using the provided registry key; store pairing state in the Mule instance configuration.
HTTP endpoint management with Registry achieved by registering deployed app HTTP endpoints with the paired Registry on deployment and unregistering on undeployment.
Dynamic lookup component implemented as a Mule message processor that resolves target endpoint URIs via Registry dynamic endpoint resolution API.
Throttling policies enforced using a token-bucket rate limiter interceptor on flow endpoints, with policies pulled from the Registry.
Business event and transaction ID logging added at DEBUG level in the existing BusinessEvent notification mechanism.
Upgrade MVEL by updating Maven dependency to 2.1.8 and refactoring any deprecated or changed API usages in DataMapper and expression evaluators.
JDBC connectivity simplified by providing database-specific default DataSource factory beans and connection templates for Oracle, PostgreSQL, Sybase, MS SQL Server, and DB2.
JDBC query logging implemented via a PreparedStatement proxy that logs SQL strings at DEBUG level when enabled.
assumptions: External wiki specifications (Registry interaction, Dynamic Router) are accessible and provide sufficient API details; we implement to typical REST contracts.
Only client-side changes in Mule ESB are required; the Registry server and its APIs already exist.
MySQL JDBC support is already complete; only the other five listed databases need new templates.
Test instances of the Registry and each relational database are available for development and integration testing.
Effort estimates include coding, unit testing, and local integration testing performed by the same developer.
No end-user documentation beyond basic configuration examples and inline Javadoc is required.
The developer is familiar with Mule internals, Java, Maven, and standard testing frameworks, so no training time is included.
